The '''1740 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 18th edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[Seytinemas]] across [[Mahea]], and was won by [[New Misos]], who defeated [[Lycroa]] 2-1 in the final.

The 1740 edition was the first FLLA World Cup held in [[Mahea]], hosted by [[Seytinemas]], and the first contested by the present field of thirty-two teams. The expansion was approved by the FLLA Council in 1737 and was accompanied by the introduction of a four-pot seeded draw and a standardised group-stage format that has since remained substantially unchanged. The final at the Vulna Olympic Stadium, won 2-1 by [[New Misos]] over [[Lycroa]], was the first FLLA World Cup match to be broadcast by a transcontinental radio relay.
